source_note: Taxonomy, native range, habit and use categories are summarized from linked Kew Plants of the World Online records. Traditional-use descriptions report cultural/documented use, not efficacy or medical advice.

Aloevera.description: A succulent perennial aloe cultivated widely; its fleshy leaves contain clear gel and a distinct bitter yellow exudate.
Aloevera.taxonomy_note: The trained model metadata uses Aloe barbadensis miller. Kew POWO accepts Aloe vera for the linked taxon; the model mapping is unchanged.
Aloevera.habitat: Dry shrubland and other arid settings; cultivated in many regions.
Aloevera.distribution: Kew lists northern Oman (Hajar Mountains) as the native range; the plant is cultivated widely.
traditional_uses: Kew records long-standing food, cosmetic and herbal-remedy uses of aloe leaf gel. These records do not establish that a particular preparation is safe or effective.

Amla.description: A tropical and subtropical Asian tree known by the common name Indian gooseberry.
Amla.habitat: Wet tropical and subtropical environments; also cultivated.
Amla.distribution: Native across tropical and subtropical Asia, including the Indian subcontinent and parts of Southeast Asia.
traditional_uses: The linked Kew record documents taxonomy and distribution but does not provide a medicinal-use claim; none is inferred here.

Ashwagandha.description: A greyish, branching subshrub or shrub of subtropical environments.
Ashwagandha.habitat: Subtropical settings, including open or disturbed places in some regional floras.
Ashwagandha.distribution: Kew describes a broad native range from southern Europe to central China and from Africa to Myanmar, including India.
traditional_uses: Withania somnifera is recorded as a medicinal-use plant in Kew's plant information sources. No benefit, dose or safety claim is made here.

Brahmi.description: A low-growing annual herb or subshrub associated with tropical and subtropical regions; it can grow in wet places.
Brahmi.habitat: Tropical and subtropical habitats, often moist or aquatic settings.
Brahmi.distribution: A broadly distributed tropical and subtropical plant; Kew records it as native in India and many other regions.
traditional_uses: Kew records food and medicinal uses for this species. These are descriptions of reported use, not evidence of a specific health outcome.

Mint.description: Mentha is an accepted genus of aromatic herbs and subshrubs. The model predicts the genus-level class, not a particular mint species.
Mint.plant_type: Aromatic herb or subshrub; varies by species
Mint.habitat: Varies by species; the genus has a cosmopolitan distribution and many mints grow in moist habitats.
Mint.distribution: Kew lists the genus as cosmopolitan. A genus-level result cannot determine the exact species or locality.
traditional_uses: Many Mentha species are used as culinary herbs; some species also have documented traditional medicinal uses. This classifier does not identify which mint species is pictured.

Neem.description: A tropical tree with documented environmental, food, fuel and social uses.
Neem.distribution: Kew lists Assam to Indo-China as the native range; the species is introduced or cultivated in many other tropical regions.
traditional_uses: Kew's referenced floras record traditional medicinal uses of multiple neem parts. This is historical-use information only and does not imply safety or efficacy.

Tulasi.description: An aromatic perennial herb or subshrub, also known as holy basil; it has cultural and culinary importance.
Tulasi.habitat: Seasonally dry tropical settings; cultivated and naturalised beyond its native range.
Tulasi.distribution: Native to tropical and subtropical Asia and the western Pacific; Kew includes India in its native range.
traditional_uses: Kew describes Tulsi as culturally significant and records traditional medicinal uses. These reports are not treatment or safety advice.
